spans.text: Dammit...
There's nobody alive in the other village either.
You look like you're searching for survivors.
I believe I've already told you that there are no vital signs in this region.
I know that.
But you might have missed something...
Tragedies are always born of necessities.
Let's go. There's nothing else worth looking at here.
ST AR-15 marches on silently with Dandelion following from behind.
For some reason, this reminds me of what happened on a certain snowy day.
Do you HAVE to bring up the past at a time like this?
And here I thought you missed our time alone together.
Unfortunately, I cannot speak to you through Lunasia right now.
That's the last thing I want to remember.
You never asked me what happened to Lunasia in the end.
I even thought you no longer cared about her.
Right now, you look like a sick little kitten that can't even muster up the strength to open her eyes.
So what?
If you want to make fun of me, I'd suggest you abandon all thoughts of that.
That was not my intention.
At least, your present self no longer holds that sort of value.
What do you mean?
I often contemplate the final stage of Doll evolution.
But no matter what, a factor that precipitates evolution is necessary to reach such a state.
Which is why I wonder if a Doll that lacks independence like yourself possesses the potential for such evolution.
...What the hell are you saying? I didn't understand a single word of that.
It sounds like you're trying to pick a fight, but I'm not going to give you the satisfaction.
I am simply saying what comes to mind. After all, I've gained an understanding of the AR Team after my time with you.
SOP-II's neural cloud is quite special among Dolls, and RO's is extremely resilient.
When you think about it, you're the only one who's prone to sentimentality.
Sentimentality? You're calling me sentimental?
ST AR-15 grinds to a halt, and Dandelion stops in her tracks behind her.
What the hell are you trying to say?
If you've got a problem with me, then spit it out, right here and right now.
Don't you feel that right now, you're like a little girl having a sulking fit because she lost a cherished toy?
M4 is NOT a toy and I am NOT sulking.
So you DO know what I'm getting at.
You brought up the past out of nowhere and made a point of mentioning M4. Only an idiot wouldn't know what you're trying to say.
But just because I get your meaning doesn't mean I want to be bothered with pointless crap like this, especially since you're the one bringing it up.
I am simply worried that you will let your emotions cloud your judgment.
So should I thank you for this pointless lecture?
The more you act like this, the more you prove that you are insufficiently calm.
Furthermore, it also means my fears about you are justified.
You think I can't carry out the mission in my current state?
...I never said that.
However, if you have any doubts, I do not want you to keep them buried in your heart.
Hidden problems are harder to handle than a simple emotional outburst.
"Hidden problems", you say?
I see, so you think of me as a "hidden problem".
That's why you've been staring at me all this time like a stalker.
I thought we had come to a consensus on this.
Can't you tell how I feel just by looking into my neural cloud?
Do you HAVE to put me through this farce of making me say it personally?
I won't do that, because I promised Lunasia that I would take care of all of you.
If she were in my place, she would be equally concerned about you.
You don't need to pretend to be M4.
You don't need to pretend that you're fine either.
...Humph.
Frankly speaking, I don't trust you in the least.
But if M4 thinks you're not an enemy, then I'm going to consider you an aide for the moment.
Don't get me wrong, though. I haven't acknowledged you as one of us yet.
And you'd better not expect me to treat you the way I treat M4.
Not even if you look like her or come from the same neural cloud.
To me, M4 is M4, and nobody can take her place.
I can endure anything if it means I can find her again.
So put your attention where it should be, because if you miss out on an important clue while you're worrying about something so pointless...
I promise you - I'll make you regret spouting all that nonsense.
...To be honest, I'm quite surprised.
You're stronger than I thought.
Think what you want, I don't care.
While all of Persica's Dolls have their own quirks, you are all fundamentally the same.
Unfortunately, I am no exception to that.
Can we end this pointless conversation and focus on the mission?
I am glad to be of service.
We've got a pile of corpses here too. Can you glean anything from them?
There's no doubt they died of radiation poisoning.
The question is...where did that radiation come from?
These people lived here, which means that the radiation levels here weren't fatal.
Our scans told us as much.
So it was a brief radiation spike...
Doesn't that sound familiar?
I found something even more familiar.
Recognize these?
White flower petals.
They're all over the place.
This region is on the Green Zone's border.
Do you know what this means?
I don't know. You tell me.
It means that William's ambitions are becoming increasingly unbridled.
The scope of his experiments are broader than we knew. He must be planning a larger scheme.
...William.
It's always that damn guy.
Shhh.
Someone's coming.
A set of quiet footsteps approaches.
ST AR-15 turns to the side and a Strelet suddenly comes into view.
...Paradeus?!
Go. Draw their attention, just like before.
What do you have in mind?
The same old trick, of course. I'm going to dig more information out of their nearly-decayed brains.
Fully armed and equipped, ST AR-15 holds the upper hand in the ensuing battle and easily defeats the opposition.
These familiar enemies now lie before her, but for some reason the sight sends a chill down her spine.
They're all dead.
...But what is Paradeus doing here?
These are freshly made Paradeus units.
What do you mean?
From their neural records, these white soldiers used to be local residents not long ago.
That's certainly not something I expected to see.
There's an automated machine in the center of the village and a few autonomous first-gen Dolls. My guess is that Paradeus is using them to turn the corpses into Strelets.
Note these coordinates so the Commander can send someone to recover this equipment.
It's nothing but blood and human body parts everywhere.
...Just looking at it makes me want to throw up.
Fortunately, Dolls can't throw up.
I can't say the same for the Commander, though. Remember to submit your visual logs as well.
Tsk... Every single word that comes out of you pisses me off.
I humbly accept your praise for my linguistics systems.
Alright, there's nothing else worth investigating here.
This mission wasn't as simple as I expected...
Since when have you ever been given simple missions?
Humph...
Let's hurry and catch up with RO and the others. I don't want to stay here any longer than I have to.
